title: Networks, I/O and the long run
dek: After runc start, Docker is byte pipelines and small state machines, and both lose or block more than users assume. This last part of a four-part teardown follows -p 8080:80 through netfilter and docker-proxy, finds the DNS server at 127.0.0.11 running inside dockerd, takes apart the 8-byte frame behind attach and logs, times docker stop to its SIGKILL, shows how docker kill -s HUP can switch off a restart policy, reads health, OOM, stats and events as thin readers over cgroup files and in-memory rings, tells thirteen years of moving work out of one binary, and ends with the register of all 100 findings.
byline: 23 October 2026 · Subject: moby@0367cbeb (Docker Engine 29.9.2) · Part 4 of 4 · Read from the source and the specs; measured where this machine allows
description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 4: port publishing as DNAT plus docker-proxy, the iptables and nftables chains, the embedded DNS server at 127.0.0.11, the stdcopy frame and the log pipeline, stop, kill and restart policies, health, OOM, stats and events, the 2013-2026 history, and the full register of 100 findings.
og_description: Part 4 of a four-part Docker teardown at Engine 29.9.2 (0367cbeb): -p 8080:80 as a bound-but-deaf socket, a kernel DNAT and a docker-proxy for loopback and hairpin, moby's golden iptables and nftables rules, 127.0.0.11 as a dockerd goroutine behind NAT in your netns, the 8-byte stdcopy frame, blocking and unbounded logs, the 10-second SIGKILL, docker kill -s HUP disabling unless-stopped (D77), OOMKilled and CPU % as thin readers, thirteen years of history, and 100 verified findings.
